articles.title: Axpo completes first LNG bunkering of containership in Valencia
articles.summary: Axpo has completed its first liquefied natural gas (LNG) bunkering operation at the Port of Valencia, Spain, supplying a container vessel with a fuel mix containing more than 50% bio-LNG. The ship-to-ship operation took place on 13 October 2026 using Axpo’s Alisios bunkering vessel, which has a capacity of 12,500 m³....
articles.body: Axpo has completed its first liquefied natural gas (LNG) bunkering operation at the Port of Valencia, Spain, supplying a container vessel with a fuel mix containing more than 50% bio-LNG. The ship-to-ship operation took place on 13 October 2026 using Axpo’s Alisios bunkering vessel, which has a capacity of 12,500 m³. The operation marks Axpo’s entry into LNG bunkering at Valencia, making it the fourth Spanish port where the company has provided the service. Previous operations took place in Málaga, Algeciras and Barcelona. The container vessel belongs to a major international transport and logistics company, although Axpo has not disclosed its name or the volume of fuel delivered. Expanding LNG bunkering services in Spain The latest operation forms part of Axpo’s expansion across major Mediterranean ports, where demand for alternative marine fuels is supporting the development of new bunkering services. The company launched Alisios in March 2026 at the Port of Huelva. The vessel operates along the southern Iberian coast, providing LNG and bio-LNG bunkering services to commercial ships. “As Spain’s largest port for container traffic and the fifth-busiest container port in Europe, Valencia is a strategically important location,” said Daniele Corti, Head of Small-Scale LNG at Axpo. Bio-LNG is produced from organic materials, including agricultural residues, biomass and waste. It can be used in LNG-powered vessels and offers potential lifecycle emissions benefits, depending on its production and supply chain. Growing presence across the Mediterranean Axpo began LNG bunkering operations in Málaga in April 2025 before expanding to Algeciras, Sines in Portugal and Barcelona. The US company acquired uranium hexafluoride (UF₆), enriched to 4.95% uranium-235, from WMC. The material is currently stored at a nuclear fuel...
articles.body: Bluecore Energy has purchased low-enriched uranium for its first maritime nuclear energy system, marking progress in its plans to develop floating nuclear power technology. The US company acquired uranium hexafluoride (UF₆), enriched to 4.95% uranium-235, from WMC. The material is currently stored at a nuclear fuel facility outside California. It will support future fuel production, testing and validation. The purchase follows Bluecore’s recent US$50 million seed financing. The company is also working with US regulators and the American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) as it develops its first system. Bluecore advances regulatory and certification work Bluecore began preliminary discussions with the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) in August 2026. The company presented its initial design and discussed the regulatory requirements for future deployment. The US Coast Guard also participated in the meeting. In June, Bluecore received Approval in Principle (AiP) from ABS for its floating nuclear power plant design. According to the company, this was the first such approval for a US-designed floating nuclear power plant. The approval provides a framework for further technical development. However, it does not represent final certification or permission to operate. Bluecore is now progressing with engineering, fuel qualification and safety assessments. These activities will support the next stages of testing and regulatory review. Floating nuclear power for ports and coastal facilities Bluecore is developing its technology at its headquarters within the Port of Long Beach. The company is currently working on a reactor module prototype that does not contain nuclear fuel. Its compact, water-cooled systems are being designed for installation on floating platforms. articles.title: ABS and US Department of Energy partner on maritime nuclear technology
articles.summary: The American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) and the US Department of Energy (DOE) have signed a memorandum of understanding to advance the development of nuclear technology for commercial maritime applications. The agreement covers nuclear-powered vessels, floating nuclear power facilities and the infrastructure required...
articles.body: The American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) and the US Department of Energy (DOE) have signed a memorandum of understanding to advance the development of nuclear technology for commercial maritime applications. The agreement covers nuclear-powered vessels, floating nuclear power facilities and the infrastructure required to support their operation. It also aims to strengthen US shipbuilding capabilities and examine how advanced nuclear systems could be safely introduced into the maritime industry. The partnership will focus on technical and feasibility studies, including the potential development of nuclear-powered shipping routes and floating power solutions. It will also examine the requirements for ports, shipyards and other facilities involved in building and maintaining nuclear-powered maritime assets. Cooperation on technology and maritime infrastructure Under the agreement, ABS will work with the DOE’s Office of Nuclear Energy on technical, regulatory, economic and policy assessments. The classification society will also co-manage the Maritime Nuclear Applications Group (MNAG), supporting coordination between government agencies and industry stakeholders. Additional activities will be coordinated through the US Maritime Administration’s Center for Maritime Innovation, where ABS serves as Secretariat. “Advanced nuclear technology is moving from concept to application, and the maritime industry needs to be ready for it,” said John McDonald, Chairman and CEO of ABS. The cooperation builds on ABS’s existing work in maritime nuclear technology, including the publication of classification rules for floating nuclear power plants and approvals in principle for several nuclear-related projects. articles.title: DHL expands healthcare cold chain network with six new air corridors
articles.summary: DHL Global Forwarding has expanded its healthcare cold chain network with six new dedicated air cargo corridors connecting Europe and North America with major pharmaceutical markets across Asia. The expansion is designed to improve the transportation of temperature-sensitive healthcare products, including...
articles.body: DHL Global Forwarding has expanded its healthcare cold chain network with six new dedicated air cargo corridors connecting Europe and North America with major pharmaceutical markets across Asia. The expansion is designed to improve the transportation of temperature-sensitive healthcare products, including pharmaceuticals, vaccines, biologics and clinical trial materials. It also provides customers with additional routing options and access to temperature-controlled air freight capacity. The six new corridors connect Liège with Shanghai, Brussels with Shanghai and Singapore, and Cincinnati with Singapore, Tokyo Narita and Seoul Incheon. Strengthening temperature-controlled air cargo operations The new connections form part of DHL Health Logistics’ Cold Chain Network, which combines dedicated healthcare corridors with specialized handling procedures and temperature-controlled infrastructure. Most flights supporting the corridors operate within DHL’s own air network, reducing the number of cargo handovers and allowing greater control over shipment conditions. DHL uses Boeing 777 freighters with three compartments that can be configured for different temperature requirements. The network also incorporates thermal blankets and validated handling procedures to limit temperature exposure during cargo transfers. “These new corridors further expand our Cold Chain Network into strategically important healthcare markets across Asia,” said Henk Venema, Global Head of Air Freight at DHL Global Forwarding. The expansion follows the introduction of a Brussels–Cincinnati healthcare air corridor earlier this year. articles.body: CEVA Almajdouie Logistics and Port of NEOM are working together to strengthen multimodal freight connections between the Red Sea and inland markets across the Middle East. The collaboration aims to improve cargo movements between Europe, Egypt, the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries and Iraq by combining maritime access with road transport, warehousing and customs services. The initiative brings together Port of NEOM’s location on the Red Sea and CEVA Almajdouie Logistics’ regional trucking network, cross-border transport capabilities and customs brokerage services. Connecting maritime and inland transport networks The collaboration focuses on improving cargo movement beyond the port by linking maritime services with inland logistics infrastructure. The partners aim to support several cargo segments, including containerized freight, RoPax traffic, bulk and general cargo, as well as heavy-lift and project shipments. Bonded warehousing and customs clearance services are also expected to support cross-border movements, providing customers with additional options for transporting goods between regional and international markets. “Connecting maritime gateways directly to high-capacity inland networks is critical to modern supply chain resilience,” said Stefano Pollotti, CEO of CEVA Almajdouie Logistics. The initiative could also support the movement of oversized equipment and infrastructure components through specialized inland transport services. By combining port access with regional distribution capabilities, the partners intend to improve connectivity between maritime routes and destinations across Saudi Arabia and neighboring markets. articles.title: Lloyd’s Register and Sagar Defence partner on maritime autonomy certification
articles.summary: Lloyd’s Register (LR) and Sagar Defence Engineering Limited (SDEL) have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to support the certification and regulatory acceptance of autonomous and remotely operated maritime systems. The collaboration aims to establish practical procedures for assessing the safety and...
articles.body: Lloyd’s Register (LR) and Sagar Defence Engineering Limited (SDEL) have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to support the certification and regulatory acceptance of autonomous and remotely operated maritime systems. The collaboration aims to establish practical procedures for assessing the safety and reliability of autonomous technologies before their deployment. It will combine LR’s expertise in classification and regulatory compliance with Sagar Defence’s experience in developing autonomous maritime platforms. The agreement covers potential applications across commercial shipping, government operations and the defence sector. Developing certification pathways for autonomous systems Under the agreement, the two organisations will develop approaches to testing, verification and validation, alongside assessments of whether autonomous systems are ready for classification and certification. Their work will also address operational requirements, safety assessments and the interaction between vessels, sensors, communications systems and remote operators. The partners plan to engage with regulators, government agencies and industry stakeholders to support the development of certification frameworks for emerging maritime technologies. “Autonomous maritime capability is moving rapidly from experimentation to operational deployment,” said David Lloyd, Vice President, Naval and Government Business at Lloyd’s Register. The collaboration will also examine how autonomous systems perform under normal operating conditions and during equipment failures or communication disruptions. By incorporating safety assessments into the development process, LR and Sagar Defence aim to help operators demonstrate that autonomous technologies meet the requirements for operational acceptance.
takeaways: The collaboration aims to establish practical procedures for assessing the safety and reliability of autonomous technologies before their deployment.
It will combine LR’s expertise in classification and regulatory compliance with Sagar Defence’s experience in developing autonomous maritime platforms.
The agreement covers potential applications across commercial shipping, government operations and the defence sector.

articles.title: Eurogate orders automated stacking cranes for Wilhelmshaven terminal
articles.summary: Eurogate has ordered four Automated Stacking Cranes (ASCs) from Konecranes for its Container Terminal Wilhelmshaven in Germany, as part of its efforts to expand terminal automation. The order was placed through Eurogate Terminal Solutions GmbH and booked by Konecranes in the third quarter of 2026. The cranes are...
articles.body: Eurogate has ordered four Automated Stacking Cranes (ASCs) from Konecranes for its Container Terminal Wilhelmshaven in Germany, as part of its efforts to expand terminal automation. The order was placed through Eurogate Terminal Solutions GmbH and booked by Konecranes in the third quarter of 2026. The cranes are scheduled for handover in the second quarter of 2028. The agreement also includes an option for four additional ASCs at Eurogate’s Container Terminal Hamburg. Supporting automated container yard operations The new cranes will support Eurogate’s plans to introduce automated container handling at Wilhelmshaven. They will be integrated with existing terminal equipment to enable automated container transport within the yard. Eurogate is adopting a supplier-independent approach to automation. This allows equipment from different manufacturers to connect with the terminal’s equipment control system, providing greater flexibility as operations develop. Konecranes was selected for its automation technology and ability to meet the terminal’s operational and technical requirements. “Konecranes has demonstrated a strong willingness to support ETS-MT in further developing our operations and accompanying us on our journey towards automated yard operations,” said Axel Jachens, Project Manager at Eurogate Technical Services GmbH. Technology and future expansion The Automated Stacking Cranes will feature Konecranes’ Active Load Control technology, designed to improve container handling accuracy by reducing load sway and supporting precise positioning. The cranes are also designed to operate within terminal automation systems that incorporate equipment from multiple suppliers.
